messages:
maya: Heads-up — during the canary RBAC sweep this morning we started seeing 403s from proxy-ingress in eu-west-1 when it tried to talk to model-serving in ap-south. TLS handshakes failing with 'unknown certificate' right after we rolled the stricter TLS profile (min 1.3 + client cert required). Anyone else seeing this?
jon: I saw the same for a few pods. Quick grep shows this in the proxy logs: 
```
  time=2024-10-02T08:12:14Z level=warn msg=handshake failed peer=10.12.5.7 error="x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" request_id=abc123
```
looks like client cert verification failing. Not a generic ALPN/cipher issue.
maya: Thanks — relevant ACL change was the RBAC policy that removed the old svc-keystore role from the proxy-service account (attempt to tighten scope). Could be a timing window where rotator certs exist but keystore access is blocked.
ops-oncall: Security bot flagged KMS decrypt denies around the same time: 
```
KMS: Decrypt Deny principal=svc-proxy-eu-west resource=projects/keystore key=prod-wrapping reason=iam.policy.denied
```
We already rolled a small traffic redirect to avoid impacting customer-facing endpoints.
luis: If KMS Unwrap was denied, the proxy would have no private key to present — that would cause unknown issuer or missing client cert. Can we confirm whether the rotator wrote a new cert bundle to the keystore before the RBAC change?
jon: Checked the rotator timeline: certs were issued at 08:10:50 and rotated into keystore at 08:11:05. RBAC change landed at 08:11:30. So there was a 25s overlap where the old role could write but the new role couldn't read. Bad ordering.
maya: Oof. Ordering bug. For mitigation I'm leaning to quickly restoring svc-keystore reading to the proxy-service role and then running a reconciler that replays a keystore read across regions to ensure every region sees the new cert bundle. Can we also capture TLS ClientHello from the failed sessions to confirm client cert presence?
ops-oncall: I added a packet-capture on a replica and saved the ClientHello. It shows empty client cert extension (client didn't present cert) which fits the KMS unwrap failure.
security-bot: Alert: RBAC policy change (PR #4567) matched recent incident pattern. Related alerts: iam.audit.log contains 12 denies in eu-west-1 between 08:11:20-08:12:05.
luis: Going forward we should: 1) require a rolling policy for cert rotator -> keystore -> RBAC flip (atomic ordering), 2) add an orchestration preflight that checks keystore readability before applying the deny, 3) add KMS audit detail exports to BigQuery (we need the principal and request payload linked to role/annotation).
jon: Agreed. Short-term: restore read permission, force rotator re-run to ensure proxies have keys, and keep the relaxed TLS profile in prod but add a targeted fallback policy for eu-west->ap-south traffic to allow a brief retry with cached certs.
maya: I'll open a revert PR and a follow-up orchestration check. Assigning: maya -> revert RBAC; luis -> schema for KMS audit exports; jon -> orchestrator reconciler; ops-oncall -> validation capture + rollback playbook note.
ops-oncall: Revert PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/4592 — rolling back now. I've also added a playbook note under the 'keystore' section about ordering.
luis: For long-term hardening: propose we add a preflight that does these checks in order: 
- verify new cert bundle present in keystore across all regions (read + checksum)
- validate KMS decrypt for each affected service principal
- only then flip RBAC deny rules
I'll draft an RFC for this gating.
jon: Also we should tighten TLS config auditing: add a nightly scan that compares per-service TLS knobs (min-version, client-auth, cipher-whitelist) vs a canonical policy. If a diff is detected, automatically run the keystore-read check and alert the owner before rolling.
maya: Thanks team. Logging this thread for the incident RCA. We'll follow up in the postmortem with timeline and concrete rollout gating. :thumbsup:
